observations: Three photos show a vintage-style sewing machine in a wooden carrying case.
The machine is cream-colored with a gold-colored control panel.
The brand 'SINGER' is clearly visible on the front panel in all photos.
A black foot pedal and a coiled white power cord are placed on the machine.
The machine appears to be in used condition with some visible wear and dust.
The wooden case is open, showing the machine sitting inside.
No model number is visible on the front panel or any other visible part.
The photos are taken from slightly different angles but show the same setup.

claims.evidence: The brand 'SINGER' is visible, but 'quality' is subjective and cannot be verified from photos alone. No model or condition details confirm quality.

risks.risk: The machine may not work or may have internal mechanical issues.
risks.proof: A video showing the machine in operation, including the needle moving and the pedal controlling speed.

risks.risk: The power cord may be damaged or incompatible with Nigerian outlets.
risks.proof: Close-up of the plug end and a test of the cord with a voltage tester or working outlet.
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-functional or requiring repair

risks.risk: The machine may be missing essential parts (e.g., bobbins, presser feet, manual).
risks.proof: A photo showing all included accessories laid out, or a video demonstrating the machine's full functionality.

proof_requests: Video of the machine in operation with the pedal.
Close-up of the plug end of the power cord.
Photo of all included accessories (bobbins, presser feet, manual, etc.).
Photo of the model number plate, if any, on the machine.
response.reason: The brand is confirmed as SINGER, but the model is unreadable and the machine's working condition, completeness, and compatibility cannot be verified from the photos. These factors are critical for pricing in the Lagos market.
